newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank says 2.25 pct ERM band never applied.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank says 2.25 pct ERM band never applied.

text.p: Bank of Finland director Matti Vanhala said on Monday the bank had never applied any narrow +/-2.25 percent fluctuation band for the markka inside Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
"The fact is that it never existed even for internal purposes," Vanhala told Reuters by telephone.
"We have chosen the points of intervention, if we have been on the market, based on an assessment of what could be considered opportune regarding the impact on market psychology," he said.
"We have really never had any numerical, like percentage, limits," he added.
Some financial market analysts have said they thought the Bank of Finland has targetted a 2.25 percent channel for the markka to move around its central parity in ERM.

The Finnish unit was linked to the ERM last October at a central parity of 3.04 against the German mark. It was under strong pressure to appreciate last week, but intervention by the Bank of Finland held DEM/FIM above 2.97 to close at 2.9785 on Friday.
On Monday, overseas investors continued to buy markka and domestic exporters joined the fray, converting foreign currency earnings to markka. DEM/FIM fell 2.6 percent to graze a low just under 2.90.
Asked why the intervention policy had been different on Monday, Vanhala said: "The inflows proved to be so big ... that we thought it better to let the exchange rate absorb part of the pressure."
During the past 10 days the Bank of Finland had been intervening to keep the markka stable near its ERM central parity rate, he said.
"The inflow of reserves that the intervention caused ... was not unwelcome for us," he added. "We would be quite happy with the level (of foreign currency reserves) that we have right now.
Nearly the full amount of currencies bought by the Bank of Finland would be visible in its next balance sheet due for release on January 27, Vanhala said.
Between January 8 and 15, the central bank's reported foreign currency reserves increased by 15.7 billion markka to 52.22 billion, it said last Friday.
